As a pioneer of African Classical music he has performed with leading artists Toumani Diabate and the Pan African orchestra among others. Uniquely schooled in both Western and African Classical music he was trained as a cellist at The Purcell School and also studied the Kora (African Harp-Lute) and the Griot tradition under the Gambian master, Amadu Bansang Jobarteh in a tradition that dates back over 700 years. From this parallel education Tunde gained a deep understanding of both African and European Classical forms of music and their distinct legacies. These strands and influences have since informed his music and work as instrumentalist, teacher and international classical composer. Tunde has recorded four solo albums beginning with his seminal ‘Lamentation’. With his many travels and musical encounters across the globe, his is a story that parallels the myriad journeys of music itself – one of origins and diasporas, traditions and renewals, cycles that weave together from a single legacy and voice.
